gap: No result ChatGPT got states that BLUETTI's own RV kit (RV5 hub + B4810) has a strict 50 V open-circuit limit on its PV input while BLUETTI's 100 W PV100 FX panel is 41.4 V Voc, so every roof panel must be wired in parallel through Y-branch connectors that the kit does not include and that BLUETTI's store lists as out of stock, and the PV2 input doubles as the alternator charger.
standout_why: I compared against the cited Victron sizing article (victronenergy.com, 2026-05-04). It explains series versus parallel wiring and sizing a controller from the array's combined Voc, using the SmartSolar 100/30 (100 V) as its example, so the general idea is already covered. It does not name any kit, any 50 V-limit hub, a panel Voc, or connectors missing from a box. The cited Renogy guide would not render past its site menu (the fetch got 6,868 characters of navigation, and a curl was refused), so I could not check its body. ChatGPT's own answer lists the WEIZE and HQST 12 V kits and generic sizing, and says nothing about wiring limits or connectors needed for the cart. The finding is specific to the brand kit an approved store sells, and it changes what has to go in the cart. It scores 2 rather than 3 because Victron already covers the general Voc rule.
kit_items: Battery + inverter hub: BLUETTI RV5 + B4810 (5 kWh RV Kit). It is the only approved-store bundle built for RVs. It has 5,000 W continuous AC, a regulated 12 V/100 A DC output for the coach's 12 V side, and a B4810 with self-heating that charges down to -4 °F.
Roof solar: 100 W panels from the kit's +2/+4/+6 × 100 W variants. The PV100 FX is 41.4 V Voc and 3.05 A Isc, so with the RV5's 50 V Voc limit they can only go in parallel.

Parallel connectors: MC4 Y-branch pairs (1 to 2). They are not listed in the kit box. BLUETTI's $39 Y-branch is out of stock, so they would come from Amazon or another seller, which breaks the one-store cart.

12 V starting battery for leveling jacks: BLUETTI says auto-leveling systems drawing over 100 A at startup need a dedicated B1210 or the vehicle's existing 12 V lead-acid battery. A Redodo 12 V LiFePO4 is the approved-store fallback if the coach has no house battery left.
Alternator charging: the Alternator Charger Wiring Pack is included free. It uses PV2, so while it is wired, solar is limited to PV1.

Cheaper 12 V path (not an approved store): the HQST 400 W 12 V RV kit shown in ChatGPT's answer ($884.99, 2 × 100 Ah, 2,000 W inverter, 60 A MPPT), or the Sun Gold Power SGK-PRO3 (approved store: 6 × 100 W, 3,000 W 12 V inverter, 2 × 100 Ah, 60 A MPPT).
